Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (264)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Honfleur) · To: Frédéric Bazille (Paris) · W. ID: 8

Monet invites Bazille to leave Paris and spend two weeks with him in Honfleur, comments at length on his own work, and enquires after Bazille’s.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (3)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Chailly-en-Bière) · To: Frédéric Bazille (Paris) · W. ID: 20

Work - Monet is working on his "Déjeuner sur l'herbe". Monet asks whether his paintings were ready in time to be dispatched and whether his bills were paid. He complains to Bazille for not writing to him, as he had promised to help with Monet’s current work

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (4)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Honfleur) · To: Frédéric Bazille (Paris) · W. ID: 29

Work - Monet urges Bazille to bring to his studio three canvases stored at his house.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (5)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Sainte-Adresse) · To: Frédéric Bazille (Paris) · W. ID: 33

Work - Monet is with his father and aunt in Sainte-Adresse on the Normandy coast, in excellent working conditions. Before leaving Paris he had sold a seascape and a view of Paris, which has enabled him to give some financial help to Camille Doncieux.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (143)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Fécamp) · To: Frédéric Bazille · W. ID: 41

Artists - finding himself tight of money, Monet asks his friend Frédéric Bazille for financial help.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (333)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Étretat) · To: Frédéric Bazille (Paris) · W. ID: 44

Monet writes joyfully from Étretat, describing how inspired he feels by nature, how hard he is working, and how little he misses Paris. Being away allows him to express what he feels in painting more freely, in a more personal way.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Arsène Houssaye (84)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (St. Michel, Bougival) · To: Arsène Houssaye · W. ID: 49

Collectors - Monet reflects on his rejection from the Salon, and offers Houssaye works.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frédéric Bazille (306)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (St. Michel, Bougival) · To: Frédéric Bazille · W. ID: 54

Life/work - Monet was unable to visit Bazille, as he took advantage of the snow to 'make some studies'

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (116)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Zaandam) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 59

Work - Monet discusses in Holland and reflects on the Dutch.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (230)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Argenteuil) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 70

Life - Monet reports the death of Camille's father, and seeks Pissarro's assistance in getting payment from Duret for the painting A Hut at Sainte-Adresse

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Edouard Manet (332)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Argenteuil) · To: Edouard Manet

Life/collectors - Monet asks Manet to act as intemediary for a deal with J-B Faure, proposing Fr 5,000 for two seascapes and two works of Faure's choice. He invites Manet to breakfast.

Events.Title: Letter 72
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Collectors - Monet offers works to an Unnamed recipient for as little as 40 francs.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Emile Blémont (100)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Argenteuil) · To: Emile Blémont

Artists - Monet thanks writer Emile Blémont for defending him and the Impressionists in the face of criticism after the 24 March 1875 Drouot sale.

Events.Title: Letter 352
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Work - Signed loan document in which Monet offers 35 paintings as a guarantee for a loan of 1000 francs from Gustave Manet.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alexandre Adonis Flament (148)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alexandre Adonis Flament (Argenteuil)

Life - Monet writes to his landlord in Argenteuil, promising the payment of overdue rent.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (252)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Montgeron) · To: Georges de Bellio · W. ID: 96

Collectors/work - Due to the amount of work he has in Montgeron, Monet informs de Bellio that he will not be able to meet him in Argenteuil, but urges him to go as soon as possible to select any paintings he might like, as a creditor has already taken some works. He also suggests dragging Mr.de Rasty to Argenteuil.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Victor Chocquet (194)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Paris) · To: Victor Chocquet · W. ID: 116

Collectors - In desperate financial difficulty, Monet invites Chocquet to his house at 17 Rue Moncey to select one or two ‘ugly paintings’ for as little as 40 francs.

Events.Title: Letter to Georges de Bellio (265)
Events.Body:
To: Georges de Bellio (Paris)

Collectors - Monet writes to his patron de Bellio, asking him to make an appointment to see his new paintings, “particularly views of Paris and the flags of 30 June" [W.469]

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (144)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Georges de Bellio · W. ID: 148

Life - Obliged to remain in Vétheuil for New Year's Day, Monet sends his best wishes to de Bellio and thanks him for his support. The artist concludes by lamenting his financial situation.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (10)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Georges de Bellio (Paris)

Collectors - Monet, in complete destitution, asks his friend for a little patience to repay his debts.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Victor Chocquet (231)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Victor Chocquet (Paris) · W. ID: 169

Collectors - Monet informs Chocquet that he will be in Paris for two days and invites him to view some works.

Events.Title: Letter 85
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Health - Monet is recovering from illness and is back at work.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Eugène Boudin (118)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Eugène Boudin

Life - Monet asks the painter Boudin to borrow ten francs.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (353)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 172

Life, Work - Monet writes about an article in Le Galois which criticises the relationship between the artist and Ernest Hoschedé. Monet sent a letter of protest to the newspaper, demanding a published retraction, which he did not obtain.

Events.Title: Letter 63
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil)

Dealers/collectors (?) - Monet announces that he will be visiting Paris and could show him some paintings.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Monsieur (307) (307)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Monsieur (307)

Dealers/collectors (?) - Monet informs the correspondent that he will be visiting Paris, advising that the man can send a painting (Martin) to his Paris address, and inviting him to view some new works

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ernest Hoschedé (266)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Vétheuil) · To: Ernest Hoschedé · W. ID: 202

Life - Monet hopes that Hoschede's mother's health has improved, and sends Alice's reassurance that the children are well.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ernest Hoschedé (117)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ernest Hoschedé (Paris) · W. ID: 3092

Life - Monet writes about his financial difficulties.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (86)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé

Life - en route to Dieppe, Monet writes to Alice regarding an impending move to Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (160)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Normandy) · To: Alice Hoschedé

Life - Monet writes from Normandy expressing distress over Alice’s worrying letter, concern for Jean’s health, frustration at being unable to work despite fine weather, and reassures her about their future despite their misfortunes in Poissy.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (309)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Pourville) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 252

Life/work - Monet hopes that Alice's return journey went well, and updaes her on his own journey as well as his painting progress. He sends his regards to Marthe and hope that Michel is getting better.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Durand-Ruel (89)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Durand-Ruel (Paris)

Dealers - Monet arranges a meeting with D-R. In a previous letter published as no. 275, (Vol. II, p. 219), he writes planning to go to Paris on the 9th June, but the present letter suggests that his travels got delayed.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (347)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Poissy) · To: Georges de Bellio

Life - Monet cannot accept Georges de Bellio's invitation to lunch but will come to see him later in the day in Paris.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (348)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges de Bellio

Life- Monet describes his life since settling in Giverny where he "lives like a bear,” dividing his time between painting, gardening and boating.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Paul Durand-Ruel (101)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Paul Durand-Ruel · W. ID: 503

Dealers - list of works delivered to Durand-Ruel, with titles and prices. This is a partial fragment of letter no. 503 (Vol. II, p. 253) where it was reproduced as a reference taken from L. Venturi (1939). The letter in the CR is dated 14 June 1884, where Monet provides a written confirmation of the works he had delivered to Durand-Ruel on 12 June.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (22)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Georges de Bellio

Collectors - Monet writes to Bellio asking for remedies to cure his children’s frostbites.

Events.Title: Letter 30
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Work - miscellaneous expense accounts, prices for works, and a photographic portrait taken in Nadar’s studio.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Petit (195)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Petit (Paris)

Dealers - Monet writes to Petit arranging his visit the following Tuesday, where they would likely finalise details around the International Exhibition, which would open less than a week later.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (129)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Étretat) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 599

Work - Monet writes to Pissarro about his work in Étretat.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Léon Clapisson (386)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Léon Clapisson

Dealers -Monet chases collector and stockbroker Léon Clapisson for direct payment of a delivered painting after a pre-agreed arrangement through dealer Petit fell through.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (334)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Life - Monet plans to go to Paris for a few days and hopes he will be able to see Geffroy

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (267)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris)

Life - Monet asks for news from Geffroy, and thinks of visiting Mont Saint Michel.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (251)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges de Bellio

Monet thanks de Bellio for the loan of one of his paintings for his forthcoming exhibition at Georges Petit. The work in question has been identified by Christie's as “Arrivée du train de Normandie”, Art Institute of Chicago (W.440).

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (387)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Misc - Monet returned to painting (struggling with a flower bouquet he had to restart) and plans to visit Étretat after London, asking Geffroy to recommend books for his son.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (311)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 894

Life - Monet thanks Mallarmé for having sent him a copy of James McNeill Whistler's Ten O´Clock and asks him to also send a copy to Jean-Joseph Carriès (sculptor).

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (354)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 897

Artists - Monet is flattered Mallarmé likes his new paintings, and fondly remembers Manet, who died 5 years earlier. In the postscript, he asks about news of Whistler.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (23) (23)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (23) (Paris)

Collectors - Monet makes plans to meet with this Unnamed correspondent, Colonel Vitalis and Mirbeau. He also invites the recipient over to show him new sketches.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (24) (24)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (24)

Life - Monet hopes for news from Colonel Vitalis before his son departs for military service on 10 November.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Jeanniot (25)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Jeanniot (Paris)

Life - Monet makes plans to meet with Jeanniot and go to Le Havre to visit Colonel Vitalis.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Petit (232)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Fresselines) · To: Georges Petit

Work/dealers - In the early negotiations of the Monet-Rodin exhibition (1889), Petit agreed to organise the exhibition should he not find anything more advantageous. He was interested in organising the sale of industrialist Eugène Secrétan’s collection, which would have impeded his availability. Eventually, Secrétan’s collection sold at Galerie Sedelmeyer.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (126)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Fresselines) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Work - Monet writes to Geffroy about his work in Fresselines.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Petit (88)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Fresselines) · To: Georges Petit (Paris) · W. ID: 948

Work - Monet writes to confirm his agreement to participate in an exhibition at Petit's gallery, in conjunction with the sculptor Auguste Rodin.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (142)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Fresselines) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 963

Work - Monet writes to his friend and art critic, Gustave Geffroy, despairing of the rain in la Creuse that impedes his plein air painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (213)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2752

Work - Monet organises a meeting with his friend Gustave Geffroy and Octave Mirbeau. He also instructs Geffroy on the timing of his preface for the Monet-Rodin exhibition catalogue: Geffroy wrote Rodin’s preface, whereas Mirbeau wrote Monet’s.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hamman (120)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Hamman · W. ID: 2754

Artists - Monet writes about preparations for the exhibition with Rodin at Galerie Georges Petit. The joint Monet-Rodin exhibition opened on 21 June 1889 and featured 36 works by the sculptor and 145 canvases by the painter.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (260)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Work - Monet has returned to Giverny from Paris, and is planning to travel back with works for the exhibition at Galerie Georges Petit

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hamman (253)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Hamman

Work - Monet writes about the organisation of the Monet-Rodin exhibition at the Galerie Georges Petit, with the help of Théo Van Gogh.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Winnaretta (?) Singer (268)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Winnaretta (?) Singer

Monet thanks his recipient for sending him 5,000 fr via Sargent for a painting, and invites her to participate in the Olympia subscription.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Winnaretta (?) Singer (269)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Winnaretta (?) Singer

Monet thanks his recipient for her contribution to the Olympia subscription.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Paul Gallimard (31)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Paul Gallimard

Collectors - Monet tries to arrange a date for Gallimard to visit him in Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jean-Baptiste Faure (130)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jean-Baptiste Faure

Artists - Monet invites Faure to participate in the subscription for the purchase of Manet's Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hamman (340)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Hamman (Paris) · W. ID: 2766

A furious letter to an associate of the art dealer Georges Petit. Monet mentions a painting which is to be sent to [Charles] Ephrussi, before beginning a litany of complaints about Petit’s organisation of an exhibition of his work

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Petit (66)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Georges Petit

Artists - Monet asks Georges Petit to raise more subscriptions towards the purchase of Manet’s Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (46)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 1007

Artists - Mallarmé had asked Monet to illustrate his prose poem La Gloire, published in La Plume in September, but to make up for his refusal, Monet will offer the poet the painting Le Train à Jeufosse. Monet also invites his correspondent to te subsription for the purchase of Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Henri Guérard (197)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Henri Guérard

On the subscription for the purchase of Manet’s Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (47)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 1009

Artists - Monet writes about inviting Degas to subscribe for Olympia, and the refusals of Mary Cassatt and Emile Zola to do so.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Subscriber (105) (105)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Subscriber (105)

Artists - Letter to a potential subscriber for to purchase of Manet's Olympia containing the names and sums paid of individuals who have already subscribed.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Edmond Bazire (216)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Edmond Bazire

Monet invites Bazire to participate in the subscription for the purchase of Manet's Olympia

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Henri Guérard (270)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Henri Guérard

Monet thanks Guérard and his wife for participating in the Olympia subscription, noting that Faure, Cassatt and Zola refused to participate.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Suzanne Leenhoff Manet (131)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Suzanne Leenhoff Manet

Artists - Monet writes to Mme Manet expressing his admiration of Manet and his determination to achieve the needed sum for the purchase of Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (132)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 1017

Artists - Monet acknowledges receipt of Pissarro’s letter and his contribution of 50 francs in the form of a money order to the Manet subscription fund.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Thomas Alexander (?) Harrison (271)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Thomas Alexander (?) Harrison

Monet invites Mr Harrison to participate in the Olympia subscription.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Edmond Bazire (145)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Edmond Bazire

Artists - Monet acknowledges receipt of art critic Edmond Bazire's contribution of 25fr to the subscription for the purchase of Manet's Olympia

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Subscriber (106) (106)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Subscriber (106)

Artists - Monet acknowledged receipt of a sum of 500 fr for the purchase of Olympia from a donor who wished to remain incognito

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (349)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges de Bellio

Misc - Monet sends New Year wishes, shares family news (including health concerns), and recalls recent dinners in Paris with Caillebotte. He then reflects on his ongoing struggles with painting, his “greatest and incurable affliction", mentions Renoir’s recent work, and offers a copy of a photograph of himself taken in the fields.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jean-François Raffaëlli (233)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jean-François Raffaëlli

Monet thanks Raffaelli for his contribution to the Olympia subscription. Includes a list of subscribers and their contributions.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (6)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1027

Artists - Monet writes about the subscription for the purchase of Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Octave Uzanne (102)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Octave Uzanne

Life - on 29 Jan 1890 Monet and Uzanne attended a banquet in honour of their friend Maurice Bouchor, and in this letter the artist expresses his excitement about joining Bouchor’s friend at the celebration.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (273)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Printed notice collecting funds promised by Gustave Geffroy towards the purchase of Manet’s Olympia. Only the signature, amount, and Geffroy's name are in Monet’s hand.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Jeanniot (17)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Georges Jeanniot

Artists - Monet confirms receipt of Jeanniot’s contribution to the purchase of Édouard Manet’s Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Suzanne Leenhoff Manet (107)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Suzanne Leenhoff Manet

Artists - Monet plans to go and see her the next day to give her part of the sum he received for the purchase of the Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Roger Jourdain (272)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Roger Jourdain

Monet records the receipt of 100 francs from the artist Roger Jourdain (1845-1918) towards the purchase of Manet’s Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Singer Winnaretta (356)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Singer Winnaretta

Olympia subscription - Monet asks Singer to send the amount she had registered under (FF 2k, the highest amount donated by a single subscriber), as he plans to hand over the subscription amounts to Mme Manet in the following days.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jacques-Emile Blanche (308)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jacques-Emile Blanche

Work/artists - Monet writes to acknowledge Blanche's donation of 500 francs to the fund to purchase Manet's Olympia

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Singer Winnaretta (357)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Singer Winnaretta

Olympia subscription - Monet sends word that the work was in the possession of the subscribers.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jean-Charles Cazin (123)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jean-Charles Cazin

Artists - Monet acknowledges receipt of Cazin's payment for the subscription to purchase Édouard Manet’s Olympia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (167)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2783

Artists - Monet writes expressing concern over the lack of news from Camille Pelletan regarding efforts to have Olympia donated to the State.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (234)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé (Paris) · W. ID: 1073

An inconvenient period in Monet’s personal life has prevented him and Alice from trying the recipes sent by Mallarmé’s family.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (141)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2792

Artists - Housework and an impending visit to his brother in Rouen prevent Monet from going to London with Geffroy. The artist asks his friend if he will attend the inauguration of Flaubert's monument. This letter is partially recorded in W.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (355)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Work - Monet writes to Geffroy about working on his Haystacks paintings during a splendid period of snowy weather.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (312)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 1089

Life/family - Monet discusses Jean's health and the effort to get him a leave of absence from military service

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Stéphane Mallarmé (313)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Stéphane Mallarmé · W. ID: 1089

Life/family - Monet discusses the response from the General, which offered Jean three months' leave in return for a demotion

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (62)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2800

Collectors - on meeting a collector interested in a ‘Haystack’ painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (168)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2809

Family - Monet writes seeking support for his son Jean, whose poor health was disregarded during military service review, and asks for Clemenceau’s intervention to secure a favourable outcome.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (133)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2812

Artists - Monet plans to visit Octave Mirbeau and invites Geffroy to join.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (134)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2815

Garden - Monet is busy with the garden after acquiring the Clos of Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (169)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2816

Artists - Monet plans to visit Mirbeau with Geffroy.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (16)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2822

Artists - Monet congratulates Geffroy on the American painter James Whistler.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Knoedler (196)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Knoedler · W. ID: 2826

Dealers - Monet attempts to strike a deal with Knoedler regarding the price of a painting in their possession.

Events.Title: Letter 65
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Dealers (?) - Monet acknowledges receipt of a check for two paintings and confirms that he will deliver more soon.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (32)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges de Bellio

Collectors - Monet is disappointed that Bellio sold works from his collection without letting him know.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges de Bellio (159)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges de Bellio

Collectors - Monet writes to Bellio, expressing disappointment at not being informed of the sale of certain paintings.

Events.Title: Letter 276
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

A list of sales in Monet's hand to Boussod, Valadon et Cie., to Bertha Potter Palmer, and to Tadamasa Hayashi

Events.Title: Letter 277
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

A list of sales in Monet's hand to Boussod, Valadon et Cie., Paul Durand-Ruel and Isidore Montaignac

Events.Title: Claude Monet to W. Hamman (217)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: W. Hamman · W. ID: 2851

Monet thanks Hamman for sending him a translation of an American journal article, and worries that Knoedler was affected by it, in light of Mr (Potter) Palmer returning two paintings to Knoedler. He asks Hamman to find out about the returned paintings are, and says that he will be in Rouen the next day.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (48)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1136

Work - on his struggles with the Rouen Cathedral series.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (218)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2854

Work - Monet informs his friend of the impending interruption of his work on the Rouen Cathedral to go to Paris for the opening of his exhibition at Galerie Durand-Ruel [Monet: Série des peupliers des bords de l’Epte, February-March 1892]. He proposes they lunch together during his brief stay in Paris.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (161)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1139

Life - Monet warns Alice about a potential relationship between Suzanne and the American painter Theodore Butler, expressing strong mistrust of foreign suitors.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (162)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1142

Work - Monet managed to work despite a lingering throat issue, and notes that if the stormy weather continues, he will return to Giverny the next day.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (274)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1144

Work - Monet writes about reworking all his canvases in the changeable Rouen weather.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice(or Monet family) Hoschedé (71)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice(or Monet family) Hoschedé · W. ID: 1149

Work - most probably sent to members of his own family, at the time Monet was at Rouen painting the Rouen Cathedral series.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hamman (388)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Hamman

Dealers - Still working intensively in Rouen, Monet refuses to promise first viewing rights, insisting he will only sell after reviewing and retouching his canvases at Giverny — though Hamann is welcome to view them without any commitment.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (170)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris)

Work - Monet is unsettled by weather and distractions while working on a new view of the cathedral, and asks Geffroy to excuse him to Rollinat and Mirbeau as he plans to spend Sunday with Jean before his departure to Alsace.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (147)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2860

Work - The spring of 1892 found Monet plagued by a sense of failure after a winter spent working on the Rouen Cathedral series.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (235)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2867

Life - Monet informs his friend about his intimate wedding to Alice Hoschedé, which they had to hasten ahead of Suzanne’s marriage to Theodore Butler.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Camille Pissarro (275)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Camille Pissarro · W. ID: 1161

Life/Friends - Monet makes arrangements for a visit from Pissarro the following week, congratulates Lucien on his marriage

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (199)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2873

Life - Monet apologises to Geffroy for not having thanked him earlier and expresses his desire to see Geffroy in Paris.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (198)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2879

Life - Monet confirms details of their upcoming meeting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hamman (358)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Hamman · W. ID: 2883

Dealers - Monet apologizes to Maurice Hamman for a receipt that failed to arrive and sends a replacement to ensure the transaction is properly recorded.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (395)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1175

Work, life - Monet writes enthusiastically from Rouen after quickly settling in and beginning work on two new cathedral canvases, feeling optimistic about his project. Alongside his painting, he visits the botanical gardens, discusses plants and gardening for the children at Giverny, and expresses his emotional need for long letters from Alice while living alone away from home.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to M. Clerc (278)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: M. Clerc

Monet writes to Clerc, a civil engineer at Vernon, about his plans to establish his water garden at Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (163)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1185

Work - Monet writes to say he will remain in Rouen due to the fine weather and pressing work, gives instructions for tasks and planting at Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (279)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1186

Events.Title: Claude Monet to M. Clerc (49)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: M. Clerc

Garden - Monet asks to meet Clerc, an engineer, at Giverny to discuss the construction of his water garden.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (164)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé

Work - Monet writes to Alice describing the dreadful, changeable weather in Rouen.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (396)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1188

Work, life - Monet writes from Rouen discouraged by unstable weather that is hindering his work on the cathedral paintings, though he remains determined not to give up. Alongside artistic frustrations, he discusses gardening matters at Giverny and expresses concern for Alice’s leg and Suzanne’s health.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (165)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1189

Work - Monet writes in frustration over the persistent bad weather, clinging to hope for improvement with the new moon, and explains how exhausting it is to keep reworking his canvases as the light changes.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (166)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1193

Work - Monet frustratedly writes about the ongoing complications with development work at Giverny, declaring he is abandoning all plans and wants only to focus on painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (121)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1195

Work - Monet writes about working on his paintings of the Cathedrale de Rouen, and worries about his garden in Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (397)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1196

Work, life - Monet writes from Rouen about practical efforts involving a petition and railway officials while continuing his exhausting work on the cathedral paintings, managing ten canvases in one day despite physical strain. He also describes attending a grand musical ceremony at Rouen Cathedral, whose interior inspired him deeply, and expresses concern about Alice’s injured leg.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to M. Clerc (280)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: M. Clerc

Monet writes again to Clerc as he has encountered bureaucratic “obstacles” to the works on his new ponds, asking for the engineer’s help in countering them.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (201)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1202

Work - Sick, Monet states that he is sending a few lines so that his wife doesn’t worry about his condition, and updates her on his day in Rouen

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (310)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1201

Work - Monet expresses his frustration with his progress on the Cathedrals series, and asks Geffroy to visit him either in Rouen or Giverny

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (398)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1203

Work - Monet writes from Rouen exhausted but intensely productive, describing a feverish day of work on fourteen canvases and his growing understanding of the cathedral motif. Though deeply longing for Giverny and the return home, he feels compelled to continue working while the changing spring light still allows it.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (281)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1208

On Monet’s frustration and exhaustion with his Rouen Cathedral series.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (200)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Rouen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1209

Monet writes about his work on the Rouen Cathedral.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to M. Clerc (282)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: M. Clerc

Monet writes regarding troubles with his planned water garden in Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (36)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2895

Work - Monet urges him to come and visit Giverny to make the most of the autumn weather and view his Rouen Cathedral series.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (2)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2898

Miscellaneous - Monet makes arrangements for Geffroy's iminent visit.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Mademoiselle (335) (335)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Mademoiselle (335)

Monet sends 700fr to his correspondent for a large painting, for which Caillebotte will arrange shipment

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (37)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2913

Work - Monet urges Geffroy to come, this time to see the irises, and compliments him on his pioneering "Histoire de l’impressionnisme" (1892).

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (237)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2917

Monet tries to organise Geffroy’s visit, and updates him on the family’s health after suffering from food poisoning.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (38)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2922

Work - Monet expects a visit from Geffroy, and encourages him to bring Clemenceau and Rodin along, but urges them to be quick if they want to see the Cathedral pictures before they leave.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (175)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1256

Artists - Monet writes about Cezanne

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (305)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Olso) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1267

Work - Monet writes from Christiania to tells Alice about his day painting outdoors at 20-25 degrees below zero. He also notes the price of paint in Norway and asks Alice to give him a comparison to the prices in Paris.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (11)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Olso) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1268

Work - Monet complains about the weather in Norway and wishes to be in Giverny to continue painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (359)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Olso) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1270

Misc - Monet apologizes for not writing more often, describing social obligations, harsh weather, and his frustration at being unable to work despite the country’s beauty. He expresses homesickness for Giverny, concern for his garden and family, and determination to produce worthwhile work before returning home.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (176)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1271

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (399)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1272

Work, life - Monet writes from Norway in a state of deep artistic frustration, overwhelmed by the beauty and constantly changing winter landscapes that he struggles to capture on canvas. Though discouraged and tempted to abandon the trip, he resolves to persevere, finding comfort in Alice’s letters, and the hope that his work will finally succeed.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (177)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1275

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (202)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1277

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (400)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1278

Work, life - Monet writes briefly to say that his day’s work went well and that he successfully painted on three canvases, which lifted his spirits. He also expresses concern about the return of snow at home and sends affectionate greetings to Alice.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (401)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1284

Work, life - Monet writes from Norway frustrated by terrible weather and melting snow, which threaten the winter scenes he is painting. Despite these setbacks and his growing exhaustion, he finds comfort in thoughts of returning home to his family and gardens at Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (360)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Olso) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1285

Misc - Monet describes fine but frosty weather and his determination to work hard despite feeling he has lost valuable time. He expresses concern about Alice’s health, who shares news of Suzanne’s progress.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (283)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé

Work - Monet writes to Alice while in Norway to show his work, updating her on its reception

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (124)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Sandviken, Bergen) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1288

Life - Monet writes to Alice from his trip to Norway.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (70)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Olso) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1290

Life - Monet writes to Alice saddened about her illness. He tells her about his time in Christiania and the travel arrangements for his return.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (250)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2940

Artists - Monet invites Geffroy, Cézanne and [Francisco] Oller to Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (135)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2942

Work - Monet had finished the series devoted to the Rouen Cathedral and spent the summer without a brush stroke.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jean-François Raffaëlli (178)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jean-François Raffaëlli

Collectors - Monet writes that, thanks to a kind intervention, he has agreed to send a painting to Monsieur Doria [count Armand Doria], something he rarely does for foreign collectors, and expresses satisfaction in doing so, especially as some have recently tried to undermine him.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (91)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ambroise Vollard

Dealers - Monet reminds Vollard to deliver his painting by Cezanne to Isidore Montaignac, director of Georges Petit.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (50)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy

Artists - Monet urges Geffroy to read Arsène Alexandre’s latest article on Cézanne and refute it. Enraged by Alexandre’s attack on Cézanne, Monet praises his fellow artist. See letter no. 2945 (1321a, Vol. V, p. 207) sent to Geffroy on 10 Dec 1895 as a follow up to the present letter, and letter no. 2946 (1321b, Vol. V, p. 207) sent to Geffroy on 15 Dec 1895 following his correspondent’s response.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (203)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2945

Monet writes in defense of Cezanne in light of Zola's L'Oeuvre, and suggests writing an article to 'restore the facts' and praise Cezanne.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (238)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2946

Following their conversation about recent damaging discourses about Cezanne (Arsène Alexandre’s article and Zola’s L’Oeuvre, in which the protagonist, Charles Lantier, was thought to be based on Cezanne; see AH.1273 and AH.1111), Monet urges Geffroy to use his influence and refute these “false legends”.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to André Mellerio (90)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: André Mellerio

Miscellaneous - visiting card thanking Mellerino.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (256)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Pourville) · To: Alice Hoschedé

Work - Monet writes to his wife from Pourville in Normandy, on a painting expedition.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (361)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2950

Work - Monet writes in deep despair, describing profound sadness, creative exhaustion after his Cathedrals series, which he exhibited the previous year, and feelings of abandonment and hostility that leave him fearful of illness or madness. He urges Geffroy to visit, hoping his friend’s presence will bring comfort amid his emotional crisis.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ferdinand Déconchy (33)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ferdinand Déconchy · W. ID: 2955

Miscellaneous - Monet sends congratulations on his forthcoming wedding.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (384)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2957

Artists - Monet arranges plans to meet Geffroy in Paris. Responding to Geffroy's remark about La petite fille aux cerises (a painting likely by Renoir according to the auction house), Monet agrees that it is a beautiful painting, but notes that 20 years prior everyone considered it horrible. Wildenstein notes this is Morisot’s Jeune fille cueillant des cerises, but the painting was executed in 1891.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (315)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2964

Work/exhibitions - Monet informs Geffroy that the new Luxembourg Gallery will open on March 8 or 9, and discusses the layout/hanging of some of the works.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (219)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Pourville) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny)

Monet writes home about his work in Pourville.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (35)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2969

Life - invites Geffroy, Cheret and Humel for lunch in Giverny.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (136)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2971

Life - Monet cannot accomodate friends at Jean and Blanche's wedding.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (296)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2973

Work - Monet describes working fervently on the Matinée Sur la Seine and some large decorative studies that have reignited his passion.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jacques Daurelle (204)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jacques Daurelle

Monet apologies for his delayed reply, and expresses reluctance to discuss certain issues (personality, gardening) in an article for Le Figaro

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Henry Fèvre (362)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Henry Fèvre

Life - In this 10 November 1897 letter, Monet thanks Henry Fèvre for sending a copy of his book Galafieu, saying he read it with great pleasure and offers his sincere compliments.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Lucien Moline (146)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Lucien Moline

Dealers - Monet writes to dealer and agent Lucien Moline, agreeing to send two paintings to London for a possible sale or exhibition.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (363)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy

Work - Monet writes anxiously about the approaching opening of his exhibition in Paris (Cl. Monet, Galeries Georges Petit, where he exhibited various new motifs, including his Mornings on the Seine and Norway paintings). Monet admits that after looking at his paintings so often he no longer knows their worth.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (137)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1437

Artists - Monet writes shortly after Alfred Sisley's funeral and the day after the untimely death of his daughter-in-law, Suzanne (Mrs. Butler)

Events.Title: Letter 284
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Life - Writing two weeks after the death of Suzanne Hoschedé, Monet informs his correspondent of Jean-Pierre’s struggles.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Frits Thaulow (316)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Frits Thaulow · W. ID: 1446

Life/friends - Monet asks Thaulow for his support for the sale in aid of Alfred Sisley's children

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (15)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: François Depeaux

Artists - Following Sisley’s death, Monet works on a public sale of Sisley’s paintings and a subscription for the purchase of a painting to be donated to the Musée du Luxembourg.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Henri Le Sidaner (364)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Henri Le Sidaner

Artists - Monet informs his correspondent about the auction he is organising in support of Sisley’s children, and invites him to donate any artworks by Sisley he could. He adds a note of the other artists and collectors who agreed to participate.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (220)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: François Depeaux

Monet writes to collector François Depeaux about the Sisley subscription and sale after his death.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (257)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1457

Artists - Monet writes about the sale organised by Monet to benefit the children of Alfred Sisley.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Mr Durolles (149)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Mr Durolles

Life - Monet writes to a military official about the secondment of his stepson [Jean-Pierre Hoschedé] to the Ministry of War

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (221)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: François Depeaux

Monet expresses regret that Depeaux missed an important meeting ahead of Sisley's art sale and reflects on the difficulty of selecting the painting for the Musée de Luxembourg, which has drawn mixed reactions. He urges Depeaux to attend upcoming events to help ensure the sale’s success.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Petit (261)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Petit · W. ID: 1463

Artists - Monet tries to win paintings by Cézanne and Corot at auction.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (73)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: François Depeaux

Collectors - Monet invites Depeaux to visit him in Giverny ahead of his meeting with the art collector Georges Viau.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (336)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: François Depeaux

Monet is urging Depeaux to come to Giverny in connection with the subscription for the sale of Sisley’s paintings after his death

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (92)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ambroise Vollard

Dealers - Monet sends Vollard a payment for Cézanne’s The Negro Scipion (now in the collection of MASP, Sao Paulo).

Events.Title: Claude Monet to François Depeaux (128)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: François Depeaux

Artists - Monet is worried about the finances of Sisley’s children after his death.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Viau (298)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Viau · W. ID: 1470

Monet confirms receipt of paintings delivered by Viau, explaining that he was so absorbed in work he forgot to reply sooner. He also asks for news of Olivier Sainsère’s health.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Wine Merchant (321)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Wine Merchant

Monet explains that he was travelling when his correspondent's letter arrived, and places an order for seven cases of wine.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (365)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 1482

Work - Monet writes about painting in London and gifting Clemenceau Le Bloc in admiration of his political campaign.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (51)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé

Work - Monet complains of the difficulties of the London weather, and sends news of the Boer War.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Monet's gardener (61)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Monet's gardener · W. ID: 1501a

Garden - letter sent to to his gardener with instructions on what he wants to plant.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Feydeau (366)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Georges Feydeau

Dealers - Monet tactfully responds to collector Georges Feydeau, explaining his moral reluctance to sell directly to amateurs in competition with the dealers who supported his success, while avoiding an outright refusal.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (55)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1607

Work - Monet writes after a day’s work on his views of London.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Blanche Hoschedé-Monet (99)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Blanche Hoschedé-Monet · W. ID: 1522

Work - Monet writes to his step-daughter and daughter-in-law Blanche from London, apologizing for not writing to her more often, and tells her about his work schedule.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (402)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1523

Work, life - Monet writes from London hoping Alice and the children arrived safely and describing his intense work on the Thames paintings. Though initially distressed by the absence of fog, he is relieved when the mist returns, allowing him to continue painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (214)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Rouen) · W. ID: 1525

Monet laments the persistent lack of sunlight hindering his work, especially on his hospital series, but remains hopeful as he continues painting.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (183)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (114)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1527

Work - Monet writes in good spirits about his work day, especially noting on how he is planning to depict the sun in the Houses of Parliament pictures.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (184)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1533

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (56)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1537

Work - Monet writes about his London paintings.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (52)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1539

Work - Monet writes about the changeable London weather, and the reaction of George Moore to his paintings.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (53)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1541

Work - Monet writes about his exhaustion from working, and about George Moore.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (185)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1544

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (54)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1548

Life - Monet writes about his impending return from London, and a bout of ill-health.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Paul Durand-Ruel (181)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Paul Durand-Ruel

Dealers - list of paintings and prices

Events.Title: Letter 7
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Collectors - responds to a correspondent who has asked him to sign and finish a work. Monet expresses his willingness to sign a painting while determining that initials should suffice for a sketch. He refuses to rework it.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (171)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1557

Artists - Monet writes to Geffroy willing to help his friend Fèvre.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to M. Tavernier (26)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: M. Tavernier

Life - Monet writes in hopes of getting his son Michel relieved from military service due to weakness.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Mr Durolles (150)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Mr Durolles

Life - Monet asks a military official to obtain the posting of his son Michel to Vernon.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (403)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1587

Work, life - Monet writes from London after arriving safely and receiving encouraging news concerning Michel, expressing gratitude for Bourgeois’s help. Though comforted by Sargent’s kindness and inspired by London’s atmospheric views, he finds the city unusually gloomy during a period of mourning and anxiously awaits further news from home.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (337)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1598

Monet describes the London fog that kept him from being satisfied with his day’s work, expresses concern about Alice’s spirits, and asks her to thank her daughters for their letters.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (338)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1599

Monet regrets the hospital in London being closed on Saturdays, the lack of mail on Sundays, and his solitude. He gives Alice instructions regarding the garden, the house employees, and Durand-Ruel’s request for a canvas.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (339)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1601

Monet writes about his slow progress on his London. He mentions social encounters with George Moore, the limits of his rapport with Sargent, and comments on political news from the Transvaal.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Mr Durolles (151)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Mr Durolles

Life - Monet writes again to Durolles to ask him to head off the risk of his son Michel, now posted to Vernon, being transferred to Rouen.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (8)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1623

Work - Monet writes about his life and schedule in London.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (255)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1624

He discusses an "unfortunate affair" involving a Major, likely related to his attempts to get early-release form military service for his son Michel, suggesting that a situation could have been handled better and lamenting missed opportunities to intervene. He also writes about recent health issues. Monet mentions his friend, the artist John Singer Sargent, who visited him and encouraged him to resume painting, though Monet insists he has lost interest in it.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (404)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Alice Hoschedé (Giverny) · W. ID: 1625

Life - Monet writes from London in deep anxiety over troubling family news and his lack of information, expressing frustration at being kept partially uninformed. At the same time, he describes his declining physical and emotional health, fearing he may have to give up painting altogether.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Blanche Hoschedé-Monet (186)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (London) · To: Blanche Hoschedé-Monet · W. ID: 1627

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Albert Collignon (367)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Albert Collignon (Giverny) · W. ID: 1642

Life - Monet angrily protests complaints about his car driving, arguing that he is being unfairly singled out while others drive faster through the village.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Bernheim-Jeune (77)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Bernheim-Jeune (Paris)

Dealers - Monet provides the measurements for his paintings of Vetheuil and plans arrangements to get them to the gallery. See also letter no. 1649a (vol. IV, p. 359) sent to B-J on 27 Dec 1901.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (57)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1656

Life - Monet writes about the recovery of their son Jacques from typhoid fever.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Alice Hoschedé (222)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Alice Hoschedé · W. ID: 1662

Monet writes in haste about a busy household day, including errands, Marthe training a new maid, and Anna keeping well. He discusses Germaine’s planned return, efforts by Deconchy to delay it, and hopes for Jacques’s continued recovery so the family can soon reunite.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (93)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ambroise Vollard

Dealers - Monet sends payment for a statuette.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (368)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1691

Work - Monet writes in deep discouragement, confessing that he feels overworked and “finished” as he struggles with his London views, repeatedly reworking and even destroying them despite his commitment to exhibit.

Events.Title: Letter 285
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Work/collectors - Monet elucidates a picture that had been sent to him, a reproduction of a sketch. He notes that it was “made a long time ago in Rouen, before the port was expanded”.

Events.Title: Letter 236
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Works - Monet informs his correspondent that the painting he sent for authentication is in fact a fake. He also notes that, although the signature has been very well imitated, it was poorly added and very easy to rub off.

Events.Title: Letter 286
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Work/collectors - Monet declines selling his last remaining painting in the series Matinée sur la Seine.

Events.Title: Letter 75
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet

Artists - Monet is organising an exhibition of Pissarro’s work to pay homage to the late artist.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (172)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1717

Artists - Monet writes about the opening of Pissarro’s posthumous exhibition, and mentions his struggles with his paintings of London.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Henri Manzana Pissarro (152)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Henri Manzana Pissarro

Artists - Monet writes to the third child of Camille Pissarro, about his father's legacy.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (94)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ambroise Vollard

Dealers - Monet thanks Vollard for sending him photographs of/by Cézanne.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Antonin Perivier, Paul Ollendorff (205)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Antonin Perivier, Paul Ollendorff

Monet declines taking part in a raffle in aid of the victums of the Courriers disaster, and sends 100 francs

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (369)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1800

Work - Monet admits he has struggled to resume work after a long pause and feels unsettled by repeated trips to Paris, worrying that further disruption could be damaging.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (14)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1801

Health - Monet invites Geffroy to Giverny, as due to poor health he cannot go to Paris.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Clemenceau (323)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Clemenceau

Monet requests a favour of Clemenceau both as a minister and a friend, regarding planning permission for his garden with the Prefect of Eure.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (370)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1807

Work - Monet asks for news from his friend and informs him he is working relentlessly on his waterlilies, not having moved since he last visited.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (158) (158)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (158)

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (95)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Ambroise Vollard

Dealers - Monet sends a payment for a landscape by Cézanne.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Julie Manet-Rouart (45)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Julie Manet-Rouart · W. ID: 1825

Artists - Monet discusses the impact of Manet’s Olympia, which Monet had campaigned to acquire for the French nation in 1890.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Vittorio Pica (67)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Vittorio Pica

Artists - Monet thanks Pica, the founder of the Venice Biennale, for sending him pamphlets published in the Italian magazine "Emporium".

Events.Title: Letter 119
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Work - Monet had hoped to go to Paris for the opening of the Salon d’Automne but work prevents him from doing so, and he expresses his views on salons and plans to go to Durand-Ruel.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (possibly Clemenceau) (371) (371)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (possibly Clemenceau) (371)

Work - Monet politely declines an offer conveyed by Dujardin-Beaumetz (Under-Secretary of State for Fine Arts at the time), stating he has nothing suitable to sell to a museum except Le Portail vu de face, harmonie brune (W.1319), which he had repurchased at great cost. Reluctant to incur a financial loss, he nonetheless suggests a compromise price as a gesture of goodwill, reflecting both his attachment to the work and his practical concerns. According to Monet’s account book, he sold this painting to the State for FF 10.5k.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (180) (180)
Events.Body: From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (180)

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Charles Deudon (187)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Charles Deudon (Nice) · W. ID: 3099

Collectors - Monet gives some information about works of his that Deudon owns

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Hans Kaempfer (297)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Hans Kaempfer (Charlottenburg)

Work - Monet addresses the correspondent, probably a response to a request for an autograph, and includes a photograph of himself

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Vittorio Pica (68)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Vittorio Pica

Artists - Monet thanks Pica for sending him his piece on Impressionist art ["Gli impressionisti Francesi", 1908].

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (223)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1873

Life - Monet apologises for his delayed reply due to illness affecting both him and his wife, who is still recovering from severe liver attacks.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (258)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1882

Life - Monet is coming to Paris the following day and hopes Geffroy will be able to lunch with him. He suggests meeting at the Courbet exhibition at the Bernheim-Jeune gallery at quarter to twelve, and adds news of his wife.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (342) (342)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (342)

Life - Monet accepts to be part of a committee organising a banquet in honour of Mirbeau.

Events.Title: Letter 224
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny)

Monet arranges a meeting at his home in Giverny with his correspondent.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gentleman (372) (372)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gentleman (372)

Life - Monet explains to his recipient that he is no longer able to proceed with a planned trip to Venice.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (206)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1911

Monet thanks Geffroy for a book he sent, and informs him of Alice's illness

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Julie Manet-Rouart (299)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Julie Manet-Rouart · W. ID: 1919

Life/health - Monet updates Manet-Rouart on Alice's health, noting that she is receiving radiotherapy but the doctor is not hopeful

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (173)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1925

Monet sends 700fr to his correspondent for a large painting, for which Caillebotte will arrange shipment

Events.Title: Claude Monet to L. Drault, Charles Raulot-Lapointe (373)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: L. Drault, Charles Raulot-Lapointe (Paris)

Life - Monet sends 300 francs to Drault & Raulot-Lapointe to settle recent invoices and asks them to confirm receipt, noting an additional 10 francs toward a future bill. The firm supplied electrical and radiological equipment, possibly connected to the radiotherapy treatment his wife Alice was receiving for leukaemia.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (350)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris)

Life - Monet writes to Geffroy expressing concern for his ailing wife and asking him to recommend his son’s seriously ill friend to a doctor.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (389)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 1941

Life - Monet invites Geffroy to visit Giverny with Vaquez and shares that Alice’s health has recently improved.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (374)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1944

Work - Disappointed that they had not selected a suitable painting together for reproduction at the Gobelins Tapestry Manufacture, but offers to lend one of his Nymphéas (Water Lilies) for a trial reproduction.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (320)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1947

Monet thanks Geffroy for his assistance with Dr Henri Vazquez, and is happy to hear his paintings were useful to the Gobelins tapestry workshop in Savonniere.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (39)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1950

Life, work - Monet thanks Geffroy for the guinea fowl, shares troubling news about his wife’s relapse, and asks for an update on whether his paintings can be put to use despite difficulties sourcing wool.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (1)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 1952

Life - Monet updates Geffroy about Alice's health.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Ambroise Vollard (317)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Ambroise Vollard (Paris)

Artists - Monet thanks Vollard for the promised delivery of two photographs of Renoir.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Jean-Aubry (262)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Georges Jean-Aubry · W. ID: 1964

Life - Monet says his wife Alice is dying, and he will arrange a meeting once he has recovered some composure.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Madame (239) (239)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Madame (239)

Life - Shortly after Alice’s death (19 May 1911), Monet thanks his correspondent for writing and shares about his suffering.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (40)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 1977

Life - Monet records his deep depression, trying to cheer himself up with visits from friends including Clemenceau, Renoir and Mirbeau, and seeking comfort in re-reading his wife’s letters.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (41)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 1988

Work, life - Monet informs Geffroy that he must postpone his trip to Paris, mentions working on his Venice paintings for a spring exhibition.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (42)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 1993

Work - Monet finds himself in the depths of despair, altogether disillusioned with his work.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Unnamed Madame (Possibly Mathilde Adler) (209)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Unnamed Madame (Possibly Mathilde Adler)

Life - Monet thanks her for a kind invitation, which he gladly accepts despite joking about his reclusive nature and expresses his delight at the opportunity to see and applaud the Guitrys.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (211)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune

Life - Monet shares his joy at the news of Sacha Guitry’s recovery, thanking the Bernheim brothers for keeping him informed.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gentleman (383) (383)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gentleman (383)

Life - Monet informs a correspondent that a sale originally scheduled for the 20th has been postponed to the 27th. He quickly shares the update in the hope that the change will not prevent the recipient from attending.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (240)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2009

Work - Ahead of the Venice exhibition at Galerie Bernheim-Jeune, Monet writes about the last paintings he is finishing for the show, hoping Geffroy’s judgement is not clouded by his friendship.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Etienne Winter, Maurice Winter (390)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Etienne Winter, Maurice Winter (Paris) · W. ID: 2011

Life - Monet thanks Winter, Clemenceau’s secretary, for sharing positive news about Clemenceau’s prostate operation. Wildenstein identifies him as Maurice Winter, whereas IAA notes his name as Étienne Winter. Etienne Winter was Clemenceau’s secretary at L’Aurore in the 1890s and was still his personal secretary by 1908. Maurice Winter was his son, who in 1908 also joined Clemenceau’s cabinet.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (391)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2012

Life, Work - Monet tells Geffroy he is sending his latest paintings to Bernheim and will soon travel to Paris, where he expects to be very busy. He arranges to meet for lunch, proposing a schedule including visiting Clemenceau after his operations and possibly the Gobelins.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (138)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2023

Health - Monet announces the diagnosis of cataract that struck him.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Jean-Pierre Hoschedé (225)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Jean-Pierre Hoschedé

Life - Monet informs Jean-Pierre of the postponement of the public sale of Alice’s belongings to October 27.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (43)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2048

Health - Monet thanks Geffroy for his book on Florence, shares his ongoing worries and concerns about his eyesight, and asks for news in return.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (44)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gustave Geffroy · W. ID: 2060

Misc - A trip to Saint Moritz has rekindled Monet’s enthusiasm, and he plans to come to Paris to view Renoir’s exhibition at the Bernheim gallery.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (83)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (Paris)

Dealers, life - Monet writes to thank Bernheim-Jeune for a nice evening.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gustave Geffroy (287)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gustave Geffroy (Paris) · W. ID: 2074

Life - Monet writes to his close friend Geffroy, asking for news and telling him of his own depression.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Josse Bernheim-Jeune (241)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Josse Bernheim-Jeune

Dealers - Monet asks Josse Bernheim to apologise to his cousin, G. Bernheim, for not having sent him any works that he had promised.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (243)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune

Dealers - Monet informs the Bernheim brothers of an imminent package containing a modest study for their wives.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (228)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune

Life - Monet thanks the Bernheim family for their uplifting visit, sharing mood uplift after a month of confinement.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (392) (392)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (392)

Life - Monet writes to a friend expressing deep grief following the death of his son Jean and thanks them for their sympathy.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Charlotte Lysés (189)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Charlotte Lysés · W. ID: 2097

Life - Monet says he is feeling fairly well but expresses deep sorrow over the worsening illness of his eldest son.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Pierre-Auguste Renoir (244)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Pierre-Auguste Renoir

Life - Monet thanks Renoir for his letter following Jean’s death.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Friend (375) (375)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Friend (375)

Life - Written just days after the death of his son Jean, Monet thanks a friend for their sympathy and reflects on the strength needed to endure successive losses. He writes that he is beginning to feel a little better but must gather courage to face these continuing bereavements.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Georges Jeanniot (21)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet · To: Georges Jeanniot

Life - Grief-stricken Monet thanks Jeanniot for his letter following the death of son Jean, who died on 10 February 1914.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Josse Bernheim-Jeune (207)
Events.Body:
From: Claude Monet (Giverny) · To: Josse Bernheim-Jeune

Dealers - Monet clarifies a dispute over paintings repurchased from Georges Bernheim, explains that what began as a favor has turned into a financial obligation, refuses to set the compensation himself, and expresses regret for the misunderstanding and the trouble caused.

Events.Title: Claude Monet to Gaston Bernheim-Jeune (Bernheim de Villers), Josse Bernheim-Jeune (242)
